mainTopic: מעשר בהמה: the mistaken ninth animal, רבא's rule מנין הראוי פוטר and its source, and how counting works with two openings or extra lambs.
overview: This amud deals with מעשר בהמה, where animals pass one by one out of a pen and every tenth is holy. It opens with a view that a ninth animal mistakenly called 'tenth' is holy only if the real tenth lost its name, just like the eleventh. That view is supported by a קל וחומר. The גמרא rejects the proof twice: with היא הנותנת, and with the point that the eleventh comes after the tenth was already identified while the ninth comes before. So the ninth is holy even without the uprooting. Next רבא teaches מנין הראוי פוטר: animals counted in a count that could reach ten are exempt even if no tenth was taken. A proof from a משנה is tried and falls, so רבא brings the word יעבר in the פסוק, and a ברייתא supports him. רבא then works through fourteen lambs leaving by two openings, and the גמרא explains that even a count that only might reach ten exempts. Finally רבא rules that with fifteen lambs one may not hand-pick ten. All must enter the pen, and the leftover five wait for the next גורן. A supporting ברייתא begins at the end and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The ninth also needs the tenth's name uprooted
steps.stepSummary: A view is stated: the תשיעי mistakenly called 'tenth' is holy only if the name עשירי was uprooted from the real tenth. Logic supports this.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even the ninth animal is not holy unless the name 'tenth' was taken away from the real tenth. And logic leads to this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states a rule. The ninth animal, wrongly called 'tenth,' becomes holy only if the real tenth was also wrongly named. The words 'logic leads to this' set up the proof that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already know the eleventh needs the real tenth's name uprooted. This view treats the ninth the same way. If the owner correctly called the real tenth 'tenth,' then the ninth that he called 'tenth' is not holy at all.

keyTerms.meaning: The name 'tenth' was uprooted, meaning the real tenth was called something else
From it, meaning from the real tenth animal
And logic leads to this; it introduces a reasoned proof

steps.confusionAlert: 'הימנו' (from it) refers to the REAL tenth animal, not to the ninth. The question is whether the real tenth lost its title.

phrases.english: Even the ninth is not holy
phrases.notes: The ninth that was mistakenly called 'tenth'

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן נֶעֱקַר שֵׁם עֲשִׂירִי הֵימֶנּוּ,
phrases.english: unless the name 'tenth' was uprooted from it (the real tenth),
and logic leads to this.
phrases.notes: Sets up the קל וחומר

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף הַתְּשִׁיעִי אֵינוֹ קָדוֹשׁ אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן נֶעֱקַר שֵׁם עֲשִׂירִי הֵימֶנּוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the discussion of mistakenly naming animals in the מעשר count.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ninth called 'tenth' is holy only if the real tenth's name was uprooted.

steps.title: A logical proof from the eleventh to the ninth
steps.stepSummary: A קל וחומר: the eleventh has the stronger holiness (it is offered) and still needs the uprooting. So the ninth, with weaker holiness, surely needs it too.
steps.simpleTranslation: The eleventh becomes holy enough to be offered on the altar. Yet it is holy only if the name 'tenth' was uprooted from the real tenth. The ninth does not become holy enough to be offered. Isn't it logical that if the name 'tenth' was uprooted, yes, it is holy, and if not, then no?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out the logic promised in step 1. It uses a קל וחומר to argue that the ninth needs the same condition as the eleventh.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The eleventh, once holy, is brought as a שלמים, which is strong holiness. The ninth is never offered; it is eaten only after it gets a מום, which is weaker holiness. The argument: if even the 'stronger' case needs the real tenth uprooted, the 'weaker' case should need it all the more.

keyTerms.meaning: And if...; the opening word of a קַל וָחוֹמֶר
Becomes holy enough to be offered on the altar

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the step the rest of this passage attacks. Notice which case is 'stronger' and which is 'weaker' here.

phrases.english: And if the eleventh,
which becomes holy to be offered,
phrases.notes: It is brought as a שלמים

phrases.english: is not holy unless
the name 'tenth' was uprooted from it (the real tenth),
then the ninth, which does not become holy to be offered —
phrases.notes: It is eaten only after it gets a blemish

phrases.english: is it not logical that if
the name 'tenth' was uprooted from it — yes (it is holy),
and if not — no?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמָה אַחַד עָשָׂר שֶׁהוּא עוֹשֶׂה קְדוּשָּׁה לִיקְרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the logic ('הדין נותן') announced in step 1.
steps.raayaObject: That the ninth needs the real tenth's name uprooted.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A קל וחומר from the eleventh, which has stronger holiness and still needs it.

steps.title: The same logic points the other way
steps.stepSummary: Using היא הנותנת, the גמרא turns the קל וחומר upside down. Because the eleventh gets strong holiness, it needs a strict condition. The ninth gets only weak holiness, so it can become holy even without the uprooting.
steps.simpleTranslation: That very point leads the other way! The eleventh becomes holy to be offered. So if the name 'tenth' was uprooted, yes, it is holy; if not, no. But the ninth does not become holy to be offered, so it is holy even if the name 'tenth' was not uprooted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from step 2. It shows that the difference between the eleventh and the ninth actually supports the opposite conclusion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 2 said: the stronger case needs the condition, so the weaker case needs it even more. Here the גמרא says the reverse makes sense. Strong holiness, fit for the altar, is harder to create, so it requires the uprooting. Weak holiness, eaten only with a blemish, is easier to create, so the ninth becomes holy without it.

keyTerms.meaning: That itself leads (the other way); the same fact supports the opposite conclusion

steps.confusionAlert: The facts did not change, only the reading of them. Step 2 read 'weaker holiness' as 'needs at least as much.' Step 3 reads it as 'needs less.'

phrases.english: That itself leads (the other way)!

phrases.aramaic: אַחַד עָשָׂר שֶׁהוּא עוֹשֶׂה קְדוּשָּׁה לִיקְרַב,
phrases.english: The eleventh, which becomes holy to be offered,

phrases.aramaic: אִי נֶעֱקַר שֵׁם עֲשִׂירִי הֵימֶנּוּ — אִין,
phrases.english: if the name 'tenth' was uprooted from it — yes,
if not — no;
but the ninth, which does not become holy to be offered,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא נֶעֱקַר שֵׁם עֲשִׂירִי הֵימֶנּוּ.
phrases.english: (is holy) even though the name 'tenth' was not uprooted from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the קל וחומר of step 2 by reversing it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The קל וחומר proof only, not the eleventh's rule.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Stronger holiness may need a stricter condition, so weaker holiness need not share it.

steps.title: A second difference: the eleventh comes after the tenth is known
steps.stepSummary: אי נמי: another reason the eleventh is different. It comes after the tenth has already been identified, so it needs the real tenth's name uprooted. The ninth comes before that point.
steps.simpleTranslation: Alternatively: the eleventh comes after the tenth has already been made clear. So if the name 'tenth' was uprooted from the real tenth, yes, it is holy; if not, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, separate reason why the ninth cannot be learned from the eleventh.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the eleventh walks out, the real tenth has already passed and been identified. If the owner called that animal 'tenth' correctly, the count is finished. So the eleventh can carry the name 'tenth' only if the real tenth lost it. The ninth walks out before the tenth is known, so a mistaken 'tenth' can take hold on it even without any uprooting.

keyTerms.meaning: For which the tenth has already been made clear (identified)

steps.whatToRemember: The ninth cannot be learned from the eleventh, for two reasons. (1) היא הנותנת: the eleventh's stronger holiness needs a stricter condition. (2) אי נמי: the eleventh comes after the tenth has already been identified, while the ninth comes before.

phrases.english: Alternatively, the eleventh,
for which the tenth has already been made clear —
phrases.notes: The real tenth already came out before it

phrases.aramaic: אִי נֶעֱקַר שֵׁם עֲשִׂירִי הֵימֶנּוּ — אִין,
phrases.english: if the name 'tenth' was uprooted from it — yes,
if not — no.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי נָמֵי, אַחַד עָשָׂר, דְּאִיבָּרַר לֵיהּ עֲשִׂירִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second, independent rejection of the קל וחומר in step 2.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The comparison between the eleventh and the ninth.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The eleventh comes after the tenth has been identified; the ninth comes before, so their cases differ.

steps.title: The ninth comes before any tenth is chosen, and the topic is closed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes the אי נמי answer. The ninth animal becomes holy even without uprooting the name עשירי, because no tenth has been chosen yet. Then it closes the discussion with תו לא מידי.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the ninth, where the tenth has not yet been picked out, becomes holy even though the name 'tenth' was not removed from the real tenth. There is nothing more to say.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the sentence it started in the last step about the ninth animal. Then it announces that this topic is finished.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The eleventh comes after the real tenth has already been identified, so the real tenth's name must be uprooted first. The ninth comes before any tenth exists, so there is no name standing in the way. With תו לא מידי, the view that the ninth needs the uprooting (stated in step 1) is rejected.

keyTerms.meaning: nothing more (to say); the discussion is closed

steps.whatToRemember: Final result: a ninth animal mistakenly called 'tenth' becomes holy even if the name עשירי was not uprooted from the real tenth. The opening view in step 1 is rejected.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new argument. It is the second half of the אי נמי sentence from step 4, followed by a line that closes the topic.

phrases.aramaic: תְּשִׁיעִי, דְּאַכַּתִּי לָא אִיבָּרַר לֵיהּ עֲשִׂירִי,
phrases.english: But the ninth, where the tenth has not yet been picked out,
even though it was not uprooted
the name 'tenth' from it (the real tenth), it is holy;
there is nothing more (to say).
phrases.notes: Closes the topic and rejects the opening view.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the אי נמי sentence of step 4 and closes the whole discussion.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ninth called 'tenth' becomes holy without the real tenth's name being uprooted. The view requiring the uprooting is rejected.

steps.title: רבא: a count that could reach ten exempts
steps.stepSummary: רבא states a new rule: animals counted in a tithing count that was able to reach ten are exempt, even if the tenth was never actually reached.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: a count that is fit (to reach ten) exempts.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רבא gives a rule about when the counting itself frees animals from being tithed again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually an animal is exempt because the tenth was separated for its group. רבא says more than that. If the animals were counted in a count that could have gone on to ten, the counting alone exempts them, even if the count was cut off before ten.

keyTerms.meaning: a count that is fit (able) to reach ten

steps.whyThisMatters: The rest of this section is about finding where this rule comes from.

phrases.english: Rava said:
A count fit (to reach ten) exempts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the previous one was closed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Animals counted in a count that could reach ten are exempt from tithing, even without the tenth actually being separated.

steps.title: Where does רבא learn this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for רבא's source.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where does רבא know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where רבא's rule comes from. This sets up the proof that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not an attack on רבא. It is a request for a source. The next steps test one possible source.

keyTerms.meaning: from where does he know it?

phrases.english: From where does Rava know this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the rule in step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source of רבא's rule מנין הראוי פוטר.

steps.title: Suggested proof: a counted animal jumps back into the pen
steps.stepSummary: Maybe the source is the משנה: if a counted animal jumps back among the uncounted ones, they are all exempt. That shows the counted animals themselves are exempt just from being counted.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it comes from what we learned in the משנה: 'If one of the counted animals jumped back in among them, all are exempt.' The counted ones themselves are exempt. Isn't that because of a count fit to reach ten?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests a proof for רבא from a משנה. The word אילימא ('if you say') warns us this proof will be questioned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every animal in the pen is exempt because any one of them might be the counted animal. That only works if the counted animal itself was already exempt. Since no tenth is mentioned, the exemption seems to come just from being counted, which is exactly רבא's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: if you say (signals a suggestion that will be challenged)

phrases.english: If you say: from that which we learned (in the Mishnah):
If one of the counted animals jumped back among them (the uncounted),
all of them are exempt.
The counted ones themselves, which became exempt,
is it not through a count fit (to reach ten)?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a possible answer to the question in step 7.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה: קפץ אחד מן המנויין לתוכן, כולן פטורין

steps.title: Maybe the tenth was already tithed for them
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back on the proof. Perhaps in the משנה the tenth animal had already come out and been tithed for the counted ones. Then they are exempt because they were truly tithed, not just counted.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps he had already tithed (the tenth) on their behalf!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof. Maybe the משנה is talking about animals that were really tithed, not just counted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the tenth was already separated, the counted animals are exempt for the normal reason: the tithe was taken for them. Then the משנה tells us nothing about a count by itself, and the proof for רבא falls away.

phrases.english: But perhaps he had tithed on their behalf!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in step 8 by reading the case of the משנה differently.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof, not רבא's rule itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה might be about animals that were actually tithed, so the exemption could come from the tithe and not from the count.

steps.title: The משנה's next line rules out that reading
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא defends the proof. The משנה's next line separately discusses an animal that was already tithed jumping back in. So the first line must be about animals that were only counted, and the proof stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: You cannot say that, because it teaches (later): 'from the tithed ones back among them!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the pushback from step 9. It points to the very next line of the same משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists two separate cases: a 'counted' animal jumping back, and a 'tithed' animal jumping back. If the first case already meant tithed animals, the second case would be a pointless repeat. So the first case is about counted-but-not-yet-tithed animals, and they are still exempt. That supports רבא.
steps.whatToRemember: The proof from the jumping-animal משנה is defended. Its first case is about animals that were only counted, and they are still exempt, which supports מנין הראוי פוטר.

phrases.english: That one you cannot say,
for it teaches (later): 'from the tithed ones back among them!'
phrases.notes: The later clause shows that the first clause is about animals that were counted but not yet tithed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the pushback of step 9 and brings the proof of step 8 back.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading from the structure of the משנה: a later clause shows what the earlier clause means.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The first clause might be about animals that were already tithed.
steps.terutzMaskana: Tithed animals have their own separate clause, so the first clause is about animals that were only counted. Their exemption comes from the count, which supports רבא.

steps.title: The proof from the משנה falls again: מעושרין may mean only the tenth animal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that מעושרין in the משנה's second line means the tenth animal itself. If so, the first line can still be about animals that were truly tithed, and the proof for רבא falls.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe the word 'tithed' means specifically the tithe animal itself, the tenth. This reading is also exact, because the משנה says 'they must graze.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the defense from step 10. It offers a new way to read the משנה's second line, and with that reading the proof for רבא disappears.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 said: the second line is about an already-tithed animal jumping in, so the first line must be about animals that were only counted. Now the גמרא says the second line is about the tenth animal itself, which is holy as מעשר. That fits the ruling ירעו: all the animals must graze until they get a blemish, which only makes sense if a holy animal got mixed in. So the first line can be about the nine animals that were already tithed for, and it proves nothing about animals that were only counted.

keyTerms.meaning: Specifically the tithe animal itself (the tenth)
The wording is also precise this way
They must graze (until they become blemished)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two kinds of 'tithed.' In step 10, מעושרין meant the nine animals that the tenth was taken for. Here it means the tenth animal itself, which is holy. That small change is what removes the proof.

phrases.english: But perhaps, what does 'tithed' mean?
Specifically the tithe (the tenth animal itself)
phrases.notes: Not the nine animals that were exempted by it.

phrases.english: This is also precise, since it teaches 'they must graze'!
phrases.notes: Grazing until blemished is only needed when a holy animal is mixed in.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the defense in step 10 by reading the משנה's second line differently.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the whole proof from the משנה for רבא's rule.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The defense assumed the second line is about an animal that was tithed for. It may instead be about the tenth animal itself, as shown by the ruling ירעו.

steps.title: רבא's new source: the word 'passes' in the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: רבא brings the פסוק 'כל אשר יעבר תחת השבט'. It teaches that an animal that will pass under the rod is tithed, but not one that already passed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: The פסוק says 'passes,' and not one that has already passed.
steps.whatsHappening: The proof from the משנה failed, so רבא gives a new source from a פסוק. The next step explains how this פסוק proves his rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק is in ויקרא כז:לב: 'כל אשר יעבר תחת השבט העשירי יהיה קדש.' רבא reads יעבר as future tense: only an animal that still needs to pass under the rod gets tithed. An animal that already passed is left out.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
The verse says 'passes,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא כז:לב, passing under the rod during the count.

phrases.english: and not one that has already passed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the failed proof from the משנה with a source from a פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's rule that a count able to reach ten exempts the animals
steps.raayaSupportSource: The word יעבר in ויקרא כז:לב

steps.title: 'Already passed' must mean exempt by a count that could reach ten
steps.stepSummary: 'Already passed' can't mean already tithed, because that would be obvious. So it must mean animals exempted by a count that was able to reach ten. That proves רבא's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'already passed' mean? If it means he already tithed for them, do we need a פסוק for that? Rather, doesn't it mean they became exempt through a count that could reach ten? Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains how the פסוק proves his rule. He rules out the obvious meaning, and only his meaning is left.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two ways to read 'already passed.' Reading 1: the animals were already tithed. But no פסוק is needed to say you don't tithe twice. So it must be Reading 2: they were counted in a מנין הראוי, a count that could have reached ten. Being counted alone exempts them, even if the tenth never came out.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it necessary to say? (it's obvious)
A count fit to reach ten

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's source is the פסוק, not the משנה. Animals that 'already passed' in a count able to reach ten are exempt from מעשר בהמה, even if the tenth never came out.

phrases.english: What is 'already passed'?
If it means he tithed for them —
Is it necessary to say that?
phrases.notes: Obviously you don't tithe twice.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not that they became exempt
through a count fit to reach ten?
Learn from this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the פסוק from step 12 proves רבא's rule.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The פסוק teaches that being counted in a count fit to reach ten exempts the animals, even without the tenth coming out.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רבא: a lamb dies in the middle of the count
steps.stepSummary: Ten lambs are in the pen, five were counted, and one lamb died. If a counted lamb died, he keeps counting. If an uncounted lamb died, the counted ones are exempt, and the uncounted ones join the next gathering.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא supports רבא: He had ten lambs, brought them into the pen, counted five, and one died. If one of the counted ones died, he keeps counting and completes the tithe for them. If one of the uncounted ones died, the counted ones are exempt, and the uncounted ones join another gathering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that matches רבא's rule. The second case in it shows counted animals becoming exempt even though no tenth ever came out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a counted lamb died, the count can still reach ten, because the dead lamb was already counted. So he finishes the count and takes the tenth. If an uncounted lamb died, only nine are left and no tenth can come out. Still, the five counted lambs are exempt, because when they were counted the count was able to reach ten. That is exactly רבא's rule. The four uncounted lambs were never counted, so they join a later group.

keyTerms.meaning: He counts and completes the count
Gathering (a set time for tithing animals)

steps.confusionAlert: The proof is only in the second case. There the counted lambs are exempt even though no tenth animal was ever taken.

phrases.english: It is taught in accordance with Rava:
If he had ten lambs
and brought them into the pen, and counted five,
and one of them died —
if one of the counted ones died —
he counts and completes the tithe for them,
phrases.notes: The dead lamb was already counted, so the count still reaches ten.

phrases.english: but if one of the uncounted ones died —
the counted ones are exempt,
phrases.notes: This is רבא's rule: the count was fit to reach ten.

phrases.english: and the uncounted ones combine with another gathering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a ברייתא as support for the rule רבא proved from the פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's rule about a count fit to reach ten
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: ten lambs, five counted, and an uncounted lamb died

steps.title: רבא's new case: fourteen lambs leave through two openings
steps.stepSummary: Fourteen lambs are in a pen. Six leave through one opening and four through another, and four are left inside. If the last four go out through the opening the six used, he takes the tenth, and the other four join a later gathering.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: If he had fourteen lambs and brought them into the pen, and six went out through this opening, four through that opening, and four stayed there: if those four go out through the opening of the six, he takes one of them, and the rest combine with another gathering;
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a new rule about counting animals that leave through two different openings. This step covers what happens if the last four follow the six. The next step gives the ruling if they do not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each opening counts as its own separate count. Six plus four through the same opening make ten in one count, so the tenth lamb is מעשר. The four that went out through the other opening never reached ten in their count, so they join the next גורן.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't add up all fourteen lambs together. Each opening is a separate count, so only lambs that went out through the same opening are counted together.

phrases.english: And Rava said:
If he had fourteen lambs
and brought them into a pen,
and six went out through this opening,
and four through that opening,
and four remained there.
Those four,
if they went out through the opening of the six —
he takes one of them,
phrases.notes: The last one is the tenth in that count.

phrases.english: and the rest combine with another gathering;
phrases.notes: The four from the other opening. The statement continues next.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רָבָא הָיוּ לוֹ אַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר טְלָאִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new statement from רבא about how counts work when animals use two openings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Lambs that leave through the same opening form one count. If six and then four leave through one opening, the tenth is tithe, and the four from the other opening join the next gathering.

steps.title: First case: if the last four do not join the six
steps.stepSummary: If the last four do not go out through the opening the six used, the six are exempt, and each group of four waits for the next gathering.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if not, the six are exempt, and each group of four joins another gathering.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא finishes his first case. Six lambs went out one opening, four went out the other, and four stayed inside. Now he rules on what happens if the last four do NOT follow the six.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the six went out, eight lambs were still inside, so their opening could still have reached ten. That potential is enough to exempt them. Neither group of four can ever reach ten on its own side, so neither is tithed now, and both join a later גורן.

keyTerms.meaning: Another gathering, the next tithing period

steps.confusionAlert: The six are exempt even though no tenth animal was ever taken from their side. What exempts them is that their count COULD have reached ten when they left. It does not matter whether it actually did.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the second half of the case begun in Step 15
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Animals that left as part of a count fit to reach ten are exempt. Groups that cannot reach ten join a later gathering.

steps.title: Second case: four, then six, then four left inside
steps.stepSummary: Four go out one opening, then six go out the other, and four remain. The ruling depends on which opening the last four use.
steps.simpleTranslation: If four went out this opening, six went out that opening, and four remained there: if those four go out the six's opening, he takes one of them and the rest are exempt. If not, the four and the six are exempt, and the last four join another gathering.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a second case with the order of the groups switched. Now the four go out first and the six go out second.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the last four join the six, that side reaches ten and the tenth is taken. The first four are exempt because, when they left, ten lambs were still inside and could have joined them. If the last four join the first four instead, that side only reaches eight. The first four and the six are exempt because each could have reached ten when it left, and the last four wait for a later גורן.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Whichever groups left while ten could still be reached are exempt. A tenth is taken only where ten actually passed through one opening.

steps.title: Third case: four, four, and six left inside
steps.stepSummary: Four go out each opening and six remain. If the six leave through either opening, a tenth is taken. If not, both fours are exempt and the six wait.
steps.simpleTranslation: If four went out this opening, four went out that opening, and six remained there: if those six go out through one opening, he takes one of them and the rest are exempt. If not, the four are exempt, and the six join another gathering.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a third case. Here the six that remain inside can complete ten through EITHER opening.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whichever opening the six use reaches ten, so the tenth is taken there. The four on the other side are exempt because, when they left, they could have been completed to ten. If the six never go out, both groups of four are exempt, and the six wait for a later גורן.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Groups that left while ten could still be reached on their side are exempt, even if the remaining lambs never actually joined them.

steps.title: What does רבא add? He already said this
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבא needed these cases, since he already taught that a count fit to reach ten exempts the animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is he teaching us, that a count fit to reach ten exempts? But רבא already said that once!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא's cases as repetitive. They seem to teach only מנין הראוי פוטר, a rule רבא already proved earlier.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is worded as a question, but it works as a challenge, because it claims רבא's teaching adds nothing. It points back to the rule proven from the פסוק in Steps 12-13.

keyTerms.meaning: What is he teaching us? (What is new here?)
A count fit to reach ten

phrases.english: What is he teaching us
that a count fit to reach ten exempts?

phrases.notes: Referring to the rule proven in Steps 12-13

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions why the cases in Steps 15-18 were needed at all
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for רבא's fourteen-lamb cases
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rule מנין הראוי פוטר was already established, so repeating it through these cases seems unnecessary.

steps.title: Even an uncertain possibility of ten exempts
steps.stepSummary: The new point is that a count that MIGHT reach ten also exempts, even when the remaining lambs could go out either opening.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: we apply the rule only to a count that is surely fit to reach ten. But a count that is only possibly fit, where the remaining lambs could go here or there, we do not apply it to. So he teaches us that we do.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that these cases add something new. One might have thought the rule works only when it is certain the count can reach ten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the earlier case, the lambs that passed were surely part of a count that could reach ten. Here the remaining lambs could go through either opening, so each side only MIGHT reach ten. רבא teaches that even this uncertain potential exempts the animals.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (introduces a mistaken assumption)
That is fit to go here (to this side)

steps.whatToRemember: מנין הראוי פוטר applies even to a doubtful potential count. Lambs that left while the remaining lambs could still complete ten on their side are exempt, even though those lambs might go to the other side instead.
steps.whyThisMatters: It widens רבא's rule from a certain potential count to an uncertain one. This explains why all of his opening cases are needed.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only a count that is surely fit to reach ten exempts. A count that is only possibly fit does not.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even a count that is only possibly fit to reach ten exempts the animals.

steps.title: With fifteen lambs, do not hand-pick ten. Count all of them out of the pen
steps.stepSummary: רבא teaches about an owner with fifteen lambs. He may not pick ten by hand, tithe them, and call the other five exempt. He must put all fifteen in the pen and count ten out through the opening. One of those ten is taken as מעשר, and the remaining five join the next גורן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: If someone had fifteen lambs, he should not say, 'I will pick out ten, bring them into the pen, take one of them, and the rest are exempt.' Rather, he brings them all into the pen, lets ten come out, and takes one of them. The rest join together with animals of another gathering.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a new rule about the right way to tithe when the owner has more than ten lambs but fewer than twenty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wrong way has two problems. First, the owner hand-picks the ten himself instead of letting them come out of the pen through the opening. Second, he treats the extra five as exempt. רבא says all fifteen must enter the pen and ten must be counted out the normal way. The five that are left over are not exempt; they wait and are counted with the animals of the next gathering.

keyTerms.meaning: The pen, the enclosure the animals are gathered into before they are counted out
I will select or pick out (by hand)
Literally 'threshing floor.' Here it means a set gathering time for tithing animals
They combine or join together with other animals

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the five leftover lambs are free of מעשר. Getting rid of that mistaken idea is exactly the point. They are not exempt; they simply wait for the next gathering.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that animals become exempt only through the real counting process out of the pen. Picking animals by hand and deciding that the rest are exempt does not work.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רָבָא: הָיוּ לוֹ חֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר טְלָאִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is a new statement from רבא. Like step 16, it holds that animals left over after the count are not exempt and wait for the next gathering.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With fifteen lambs, all of them go into the pen and ten are counted out through the opening. One of those ten is the מעשר. The remaining five are not exempt; they combine with the animals of the next גורן.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רבא's ruling about fifteen lambs
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins quoting a ברייתא that teaches the same case of fifteen lambs, as support for רבא. The ברייתא continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: This was also taught in a ברייתא: If someone had fifteen lambs,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting to bring a ברייתא as support for רבא. This line only opens the quote, and the rest of the ברייתא comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase תניא נמי הכי means 'a ברייתא says the same thing.' It tells us רבא's ruling is not only his own reasoning; an earlier teaching already says it. The ברייתא starts with the same case, fifteen lambs.
